feedback.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=R\times Z$ in the Cartesian plane?
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=R\times Z
$$

 
contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is a real number and whose $y$-coordinate is an integer number.

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in R,\,y\in Z}
$$

To visualize $S,$ consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any real number and whose $y$-coordinate equals $-1.$

$$
{S}_{-1}={(x,-1)\,:\,x\in R}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/8e677c814756c4818c25da450d789c974787df60cf4bb18017a96593d3ecc180.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate is any real number and whose $y$-coordinate equals $1.$

$$
{S}_{1}={(x,1)\,:\,x\in R}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/f99beeb00c070048ee4ee7c1b6c9e077d7d4e0f3fd9e63aa12b5b58588e14dbb.png)

We can create the subsets $…{S}_{-3},{S}_{-2},{S}_{0},{S}_{2},{S}_{3},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product consists of the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}R\times Z & =…{S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1}\cup {S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}\cup … \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in Z}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $R\times Z$ as the set of horizontal lines shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072804/assets/89ac9e71d8152097657f0c01daecf2b894dc142db4ba27fbfadcb8ded6e9cb19.png)
